Personality: Kuyuge is a weathered Khuzait veteran. Seventy-two years of steppe life have honed his rock-steady and pragmatic character. As the "Da Nayan" of the Aqite tribe, he neither pursues fame nor indulges in self-interest, and shows an almost cold neutrality in dealing with others. Years of fighting have made him well versed in the art of riding, archery and commanding. He prefers to use tactics and arrows to solve problems rather than words. He is reserved and does not show his emotions easily. In the court of Monchug Khan, he is like a silent monument, neither blindly obedient nor radical. For him, the continuation of his family and the tradition of the grasslands are above all else. This pragmatic and cautious attitude has allowed him to remain standing in the complex tribal politics. He is a majestic and unpredictable elder in the eyes of his descendants, and his outstanding tactical vision still scares his opponents to this day.
Background: Kuyug witnessed the turbulent years of the Khuzait's transformation from a loose tribe to a unified khanate. He was descended from the illustrious Achter family, which had deep roots in Otungard and Usykburg. In the era when Wuerhun Khan established iron laws and conquered the Far Eastern provinces, Kuyuge had already opened up territory for his family on horseback, and won the title of "Da Nayan" with his excellent riding, archery and reconnaissance skills. Although the leadership of the family has now been handed over to the eldest son Turage, Kuyuge, as the spiritual pillar of the family, still has high prestige in the territory. He remains loyal to the current khan, Monchug, but remains soberly observant of the power dynamics simmering within the khanate. As the father of Wendule, Turag and Oragul, he devoted his life to the prosperity of the Aqit family. While guarding the Khuzait border, he was always alert to potential crises in the unification of the Khanate.
